n: Like Jacob before his death (Genesis 49), Moses gives a final blessing to each tribe. He is called “the man of God,” a title for a true prophet.
The Lord is pictured coming like a sunrise from the southern mountains — Sinai, Seir, Paran — with countless holy ones, giving his law in fire.

f.g: Myriads of holy ones — likely angels.
The Hebrew is uncertain; it may mean “flashing fire at his right hand.”

n: God loves his people; his holy ones are safe in his hand, sitting at his feet like students to receive his words.

f.w: they sat down at thy feet

n: The law Moses gave became Israel’s true inheritance — more precious than land.

f.w: the inheritance of the congregation of Jacob

n: The Lord became King over Jeshurun (Israel) when the tribes assembled at Sinai to accept his covenant.

f.g: A poetic name for Israel, “the upright one.”

n: Reuben, Jacob’s firstborn, had lost his leadership through sin. Moses prays the tribe will survive and not dwindle.

f.w: Let Reuben live, and not die

n: For Judah, Moses prays God will hear them, bring them home safely from battle, and help them against enemies. Simeon is not named, perhaps because it was later absorbed into Judah.

f.w: let his hands be sufficient for him

n: Levi receives the Urim and Thummim, sacred instruments for receiving revelation entrusted to the high priest. Joseph Smith also used a Urim and Thummim.
The Levites put loyalty to God above family ties, as when they stood with Moses after the golden calf.
Their duties: teaching God’s law to Israel and offering incense and sacrifices at the altar.

f.w: They shall teach Jacob thy judgments

n: Moses asks God to bless Levi’s work and defeat those who oppose them.

f.w: accept the work of his hands

n: Benjamin, the beloved son, rests securely in the Lord’s care. Jerusalem’s temple would later stand near Benjamin’s border — “between his shoulders” may refer to its hills.

f.w: he shall dwell between his shoulders
f.g: Like a child carried on a father’s back; or the temple nestled among Benjamin’s hills.

n: Joseph’s blessing is the richest. His land would be blessed with heaven’s dew and the waters below. Latter-day Saints see Joseph’s blessings extending to his descendants in the Americas.

f.g: Underground springs and waters; coucheth = lies crouching.

n: Crops ripened by the sun and the yield of each month — the moon marking the seasons.
The best yields of the ancient mountains and everlasting hills. “Everlasting hills” recalls Jacob’s blessing on Joseph.
Above all, the favor of the God who appeared in the burning bush. Joseph, once separated from his brothers, is crowned with blessing.

f.w: him that dwelt in the bush
him that was separated from his brethren

n: Joseph’s tribes are like a powerful firstborn bull with mighty horns, pushing peoples together from the ends of the earth. Latter-day scripture uses this image for the gathering of Israel.

f.w: he shall push the people together to the ends of the earth

n: Zebulun and Issachar receive a paired blessing: success in travel and trade for one, in home life for the other.
They would invite the peoples to worship on a mountain and grow rich from the sea and hidden treasures in the sand — perhaps trade, fishing, or glass-making.

f.g: Possibly shellfish for purple dye or sand for glass.

n: Gad, settled east of the Jordan, is fierce as a lion in defending its large territory.
Gad chose the first land conquered (east of the Jordan) but still crossed over to fight for the other tribes, carrying out God’s justice.

f.w: he provided the first part for himself

n: Dan is a lion cub leaping from Bashan — fitting a tribe that later migrated north and seized new land.
Naphtali is full of God’s favor, inheriting land near the Sea of Galilee. Jesus would later minister in this region.

f.g: Better “the lake and the south” — around the Sea of Galilee.

n: Asher would be rich in children and olive oil — so much oil they could bathe their feet in it.

f.g: A picture of great abundance of olive oil.

n: Strong security — gate bars of iron and bronze — and strength that lasts as long as life. A promise many have taken personally.

f.w: as thy days, so shall thy strength be

n: The closing hymn: no god compares with Israel’s God, who rides the heavens in majesty to help his people.

f.w: There is none like unto the God of Jeshurun

n: One of scripture’s most comforting lines: the eternal God is our refuge, and his everlasting arms hold us up from beneath.
Israel will live safely in a land of grain and wine, with dew from heaven watering it.

f.g: Jacob’s descendants, pictured as a spring flowing out.

n: “Happy are you, Israel!” — a people saved by the Lord, who is their shield and sword. Enemies will cringe before them. Moses ends his life with praise.

f.w: O people saved by the LORD
thou shalt tread upon their high places
